mainTopic: The ways to acquire land and movables (כסף, שטר, חזקה, משיכה, and movables along with land) and the sources for each
overview: The amud opens with the last line of the earlier discussion about lifting an elephant: it can stand on bundles of vines. Then a new משנה teaches the ways to acquire property. Land is acquired with כסף, שטר, or חזקה. Movables are acquired only with משיכה, unless they are acquired together with land, and movables can also pull land into a court oath. The גמרא finds a פסוק for each method. For כסף it brings 'fields shall be acquired with money' and explains that the document there is only proof; רב limits this to places where documents are not customary. For שטר it brings 'the deed of purchase'; שמואל limits this to gifts, and רב המנונא and רב אשי each defend שמואל against a ברייתא about a sale document. The גמרא then gives פסוקים for חזקה and for משיכה, and explains how the משנה fits רבי יוחנן, who holds that money acquires movables by Torah law. Finally, חזקיה gives the source for acquiring movables along with land. The גמרא then asks whether the movables must be piled on that land, and רב יוסף begins a proof from רבי עקיבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Another way to lift an elephant: bundles of vines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion by giving one more way to acquire an elephant by lifting it: having it stand on bundles of vine branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: by using bundles of vine branches.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the earlier discussion about how a buyer can acquire an elephant, which is too big to lift. It offers one more answer: lead the elephant onto bundles of vines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that an elephant is too heavy to lift in the normal way. If the elephant stands on bundles of vines, it is raised off the ground, and that counts as lifting it. This line closes the topic before the new משנה begins.

phrases.english: Alternatively:
by bundles of vine branches.
phrases.notes: Still talking about the elephant from before: when it stands on the bundles, it counts as being lifted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question from the previous amud (25b) about how to acquire an elephant by lifting it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An elephant can be acquired by having it stand on bundles of vine branches.

steps.title: Land is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that property that serves as a guarantee (land) can be acquired in three ways: כסף, שטר, or חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Property that serves as a guarantee can be acquired with money, with a document, or by taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the three ways to acquire land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land is called נכסים שיש להם אחריות because a lender can collect from it if a debt is not paid. Since land stays in place, it can serve as a guarantee. The משנה lists three ways to acquire it: paying money, handing over a deed, or doing an act of ownership on it (חזקה).

keyTerms.meaning: Property that serves as a guarantee, meaning land and things fixed to it
Money, used as a way of acquiring
Taking possession by acting as the owner, for example fencing or digging

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Property that has a guarantee,
phrases.notes: This means land. A lender can collect from it, so it 'backs up' a debt.

phrases.english: is acquired with money, with a document, and with taking possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Land can be acquired through כסף, שטר, or חזקה.

steps.title: Movable property is acquired only by pulling
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that movable property (נכסים שאין להם אחריות) is acquired only through משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Property that does not serve as a guarantee is acquired only by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the rule for movable things. They can be acquired only by pulling them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable items cannot serve as a guarantee for a debt. For these items, money alone does not complete the purchase. The buyer must pull the item into his possession (משיכה).

keyTerms.meaning: Property that does not serve as a guarantee, meaning movable items
Pulling the item toward oneself to acquire it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think money works for movables just because it works for land. Here the משנה says movables are acquired ONLY with משיכה.

phrases.english: Those that do not have a guarantee,
are acquired only by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts movables with the land rule from the step before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Movable property is acquired only through משיכה.

steps.title: Movables can be acquired together with land
steps.stepSummary: Movable property can be acquired along with land through the same כסף, שטר, or חזקה done on the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Property that does not serve as a guarantee can be acquired together with property that serves as a guarantee, through money, a document, or taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exception to the last rule. Movables do not need pulling if they are acquired together with land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone buys land and movables in one deal, the act that acquires the land also acquires the movables. This shows that the rule of משיכה has an exception when movables are attached to a land deal. This is known as קנין אגב, acquiring 'along with' land.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquiring movables 'along with' land (the common name for this rule)

phrases.english: Property that does not have a guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
phrases.english: is acquired together with property that has a guarantee
with money, with a document, and with taking possession,

steps.triggerLanguage: נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the rule that movables need משיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Movables bought together with land are acquired through the land's act of acquisition.

steps.title: Movables pull land into an oath
steps.stepSummary: If someone must swear about movables, the movables can 'bind' the land so that he must also swear about the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the movables bind the property that serves as a guarantee, so that one must swear about it too.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a court rule. Normally there is no oath about land, but movables can pull the land into an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a defendant does not take an oath when the claim is about land. If the claim includes movables, and he must swear about the movables (for example, because he admitted part of the claim), the court can make him swear about the land too. The movables 'attach' the land to the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Bind or attach; here, pull into the oath

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has four rules: land is acquired with כסף, שטר, or חזקה. Movables are acquired only with משיכה. Movables can be acquired together with land. Movables can pull land into an oath.

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹקְקִין אֶת הַנְּכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
phrases.english: and they bind the property that has a guarantee
phrases.notes: 'They' means the movable items. They tie the land to the oath they already require.

phrases.english: to swear about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹקְקִין אֶת הַנְּכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת לִישָּׁבַע עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second way that movables and land work together, this time for oaths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath required over movables also extends to land claimed in the same case.

steps.title: What is the source that money acquires land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking for the source that land is acquired with כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: With money, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the first rule in the משנה, that money acquires land. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule without a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that paying money is enough to acquire land.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
With money, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that land can be acquired with כסף.

steps.title: חזקיה brings a פסוק: fields are bought with money
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה quotes ירמיהו: 'They shall acquire fields with money.'
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The verse says, 'Fields shall be acquired with money.'
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question with a פסוק from ירמיהו that connects buying fields with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says fields are acquired 'בכסף', with money. חזקיה reads this as a legal source that the money itself acquires the land.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall acquire fields with money

phrases.english: Hizkiyya said:
The verse says:
"They shall acquire fields with money."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'שדות בכסף יקנו' teaches that money acquires land.

steps.title: Maybe a document is also needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the same פסוק mentions writing a document, so maybe money works only together with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the purchase is not complete until there is a document, as it is written: 'And write in the document and sign.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חזקיה's proof. The same פסוק also talks about writing a deed, so maybe money is not enough by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is the source, we should read all of it. The פסוק mentions money and a written, signed document. So perhaps the purchase needs both, and money alone would not acquire the land.

keyTerms.meaning: But let me say (introduces another possible reading)
And write in the document and sign it

phrases.english: But say: not until there is a document,
as it is written: "And write in the document and sign"!
phrases.notes: This is from the same פסוק, ירמיהו 32:44.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's claim that money alone acquires land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק requires a written, signed document, which suggests that money works only together with a שטר.

steps.title: Money acquires; the document is only proof
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יקנו' comes right after money, at the start of the פסוק. So money is what acquires, and the שטר is only evidence.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'they shall acquire' were written at the end, it would be as you said. Now that 'they shall acquire' is written at the beginning, money acquires, and the document is merely proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by looking at the order of words in the פסוק. 'They shall acquire' comes right after 'money,' before the document is mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose 'יקנו' came after the document. Then acquiring would depend on both money and the document. Since 'יקנו' comes first, attached to money, the acquisition is complete with money alone. The document is just written proof of the sale.
steps.whatToRemember: Money (כסף) acquires land by itself. In ירמיהו the שטר serves only as proof, because 'יקנו' is placed right after 'בכסף'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up how the גמרא will separate an act that acquires from a document that only records the sale. Later the גמרא will need a separate source for שטר as a way of acquiring.

phrases.english: If "they shall acquire" were written at the end,
it would be as you said,
now that "they shall acquire" is written at the beginning,
money acquires,
and the document is merely proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and keeps חזקיה's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading based on word order in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק mentions a document, maybe the purchase needs both money and a שטר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יקנו' is attached to money at the start of the פסוק, so money alone acquires, and the שטר is only proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Land is acquired with כסף alone. The document in ירמיהו serves as evidence.

steps.title: רב: Money alone acquires land only where documents are not customary
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the rule that כסף acquires land. Where the custom is to write a שטר, money alone does not finish the sale, unless the buyer said up front that it should.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The rule that money acquires land applies only where people do not usually write a document. But where they do write a document, the buyer has not acquired yet. And if he said clearly that the money should acquire, then it does.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a limit to the rule we just learned, that land is acquired with כסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where documents are customary, the seller expects to finish the deal with a שטר, so money alone does not close it. But custom only sets the default. If the buyer says outright that the money should acquire, his words decide.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only... (a phrase that limits an earlier rule)
In a place where people write (a document)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying money never acquires land. Money is still a real way to acquire land. רב is only saying that in some places it needs to be stated outright.

phrases.english: Rav said:
They taught this only
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה's rule that land is acquired with money.

phrases.english: in a place where they do not write a document,
but in a place where they do write a document,
he has not acquired.
And if he specified, he has specified.
phrases.notes: He means: if the buyer said outright that the money should acquire, then it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the money-acquires rule that was just proven from the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money alone acquires land only where documents are not customary, unless the buyer says outright that it should.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין kept both options open when buying land
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין used to say, when buying land, that he could choose to acquire either with the money or with the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב אידי בר אבין did. When he bought land, he would say: If I want, I will acquire with the money; if I want, I will acquire with the document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life practice that fits רב's rule that a buyer can 'specify' how he acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that a buyer's clear statement can decide which act finishes the sale. רב אידי בר אבין used this idea and set a condition at the start, so he could choose later which act, money or document, would finish the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this case of... (brings an example)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Like that of Rav Idi bar Avin:
when he would buy land, he would say:
If I want, with the money I will acquire;
if I want, with the document I will acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical example of 'if he specified' from רב's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the buyer's stated intent decides whether money acquires.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב אידי בר אבין.

steps.title: Why Rav Idi bar Avin wanted both options
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the benefit of each option. With money, the seller cannot back out. With the document, the buyer himself can still back out until he gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If I want, I will acquire with the money, so that if you sellers want to back out, you cannot. And if I want, I will acquire with the document, so that if I want to back out, I still can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב אידי בר אבין's words in order to explain why each option helps the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he picks money, the sale is finished as soon as he pays, so the seller is locked in. If he picks the document, the sale is not finished until he gets the שטר, so he keeps the freedom to cancel. Either way, he holds the control.

keyTerms.meaning: To back out of a deal

steps.whatToRemember: Money can finish a land sale right away. A document can be chosen as the finishing act instead, and then nothing is final until it is handed over.

phrases.english: If I want, with the money I will acquire,
so that if you want to back out,
you cannot back out.
And if I want, with the document I will acquire,
so that if I want to back out,
I can back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵינָא בְּכַסְפָּא – אִיקְנֵי, דְּאִי בָּעֵיתוּ לְמִיהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purpose of the condition from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Choosing money locks the seller in at once. Choosing the document lets the buyer back out until he receives it.

steps.title: What is the source that a document acquires land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next way of acquiring in the משנה, the שטר, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says land is acquired "with a document." How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the second way of acquiring land and sets up a search for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already have a פסוק for money. Now we need a separate source showing that a document alone can transfer land.

keyTerms.meaning: And with a document (quoted from the משנה)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: "And with a document."
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with money, the גמרא turns to the משנה's next method.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a שטר acquires land.

steps.title: The first verse can't be the source, since we said that document is only proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק about writing and signing a document, but rejects it. We already said that document is only evidence.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the source is the פסוק "And write in the document, and seal, and have witnesses testify," didn't you already say that this document is only proof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries an obvious source and right away rejects it because of what we already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 we read that same פסוק as saying money acquires and the שטר is only proof. So it cannot also teach that a שטר acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say (a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written:
"And write in the document, and seal, and have witnesses testify,"
but didn't you say
that the document is merely proof!
phrases.notes: This points back to the answer in step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A proposed answer to step 13, rejected at once.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this פסוק as the source, not the rule that a שטר acquires.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That פסוק was already read as making the document only evidence.

steps.title: The source: "And I took the deed of purchase"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different פסוק that calls the document a "deed of purchase." That wording shows the document itself acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is from here: "And I took the deed of purchase."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer, a different פסוק from the same story in ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls it "the document of acquiring," so the document itself is what transfers the land, not just proof of the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: The deed of purchase, the document that acquires

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And I took the deed of purchase."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source from step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "סֵפֶר הַמִּקְנָה" show that a document itself acquires land.

steps.title: שמואל: A document alone acquires only for a gift, not a sale
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the rule. A שטר alone acquires land given as a gift. In a sale, the buyer does not acquire until he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: They taught that a document acquires only for a gift document. But in a sale, the buyer does not acquire until he gives the seller the money.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a limit to the rule that a שטר acquires land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, the seller is not truly ready to let go of his land until he is paid. So the document alone is not enough there. In a gift no payment is expected, so the document finishes the transfer.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
They taught this only about a gift document,
but in a sale he does not acquire
until he gives him the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטַר מַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the שטר rule that was just sourced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שטר alone acquires land only as a gift. In a sale, payment is needed.

steps.title: רב המנונא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא about a sale document
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא. A document saying "my field is sold to you" makes the field sold. So a document seems to work for a sale too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: How does acquiring with a document work? If the seller wrote for the buyer, on paper or on a piece of pottery, even if they are not worth a פרוטה, "My field is sold to you" or "My field is given to you," then the field is sold or given.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא that seems to let a document alone finish a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts sale and gift side by side and says both are done with the document. It also stresses that the paper is worth nothing, so the document is not working as payment. That goes against שמואל, who said a sale needs money.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna objected:
With a document, how does it work?

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב לוֹ עַל הַנְּיָיר אוֹ עַל הַחֶרֶס,
phrases.english: If he wrote for him on paper or on a piece of pottery,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה,
phrases.english: even though they are not worth a perutah,
"My field is sold to you,"
"My field is given to you,"
then it is sold or given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's limit from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a document alone does not finish a sale.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a document reading "my field is sold to you" makes the field sold, with no payment mentioned.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about someone selling a field because it is bad
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers his own challenge. The ברייתא is about a seller eager to get rid of a poor field, so he lets the document alone finish the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection, and he answered it himself: the ברייתא is about someone who sells his field because it is poor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers his own question and keeps שמואל's rule standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a seller wants his money before he lets go of the land, which is why שמואל requires payment. But someone dumping a bad field wants the deal done fast, so he is happy for the document to finish it. The ברייתא is that special case, and the general rule stays the same.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He asked it and he answered it himself

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, a שטר alone acquires land given as a gift. In a sale, money is needed, except when the seller is eager to be rid of a bad field.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
It is about one who sells his field because of its poor quality.
phrases.notes: He's eager to be rid of it, so he lets the document alone finish the sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say a document finishes any sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about a seller who wants to be rid of a poor field. Normal sales still need money.

steps.title: רב אשי: The document was really for a gift
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the challenge from the ברייתא differently. The case is really a gift, and the giver wrote sale language only to strengthen the receiver's rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He wanted to give it to him as a gift. So why did he write sale language? To make the receiver's position stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to רב המנונא's challenge from the ברייתא. He says the ברייתא is not talking about a real sale at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא answered that it was a sale of a poor field. רב אשי says instead that it was a gift written in sale wording. Since it is truly a gift, the שטר alone acquires, just as שמואל said. So שמואל's rule stays fully intact.

keyTerms.meaning: To strengthen his position (the receiver's rights)

steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps שמואל's split intact: a שטר alone acquires a gift, but a sale needs payment.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
He wanted to give it to him as a gift,
and why did he write him the wording of a sale?
In order to strengthen his position.
phrases.notes: If a creditor later takes the field, the receiver can collect from the giver's other property, the way a buyer could.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּמַתָּנָה בִּיקֵּשׁ לִיתְּנָהּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same challenge that רב המנונא answered in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: it is a gift, not a sale
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that a שטר alone completes a real sale
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a gift written in sale language, so the שטר works there, just as שמואל said

steps.title: Where do we learn that land is acquired by possession?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה, that land is acquired by חזקה, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And by possession.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the third way of acquiring land listed in the משנה and asks for a source. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money and שטר already have their sources. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק showing that taking possession of land, such as using it like an owner, acquires it.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking possession: doing an owner's act on the land
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: 'And by possession.' From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the שטר discussion and moves to the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source showing that חזקה acquires land

steps.title: חזקיה: 'Dwell in your cities that you have taken'
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה brings a פסוק saying the cities were 'taken.' How were they taken? By dwelling in them. So living on land acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The פסוק says, 'And dwell in your cities that you have taken.' How did you take them? By dwelling there.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives the source for חזקה. The פסוק links 'taking' a city to 'dwelling' in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of cities 'that you have taken,' right after telling them to dwell there. The גמרא reads it as: the taking happened through the dwelling. So an owner's act on land, like living there, acquires it.

phrases.english: Chizkiyah said: The verse says:
"And dwell in your cities that you have taken";
How did you take them? By dwelling there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: אָמַר קְרָא: וּשְׁבוּ בְּעָרֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר תְּפַשְׂתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירמיהו 40:10 shows that cities are 'taken' through dwelling, so חזקה acquires land

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: 'Possess it and dwell there'
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל brings a different פסוק from the Torah. 'You shall possess it and dwell there.' How did you possess it? By dwelling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And you shall possess it and dwell there.' How did you possess it? By dwelling there.
steps.whatsHappening: A second source for חזקה is given, this time from a פסוק in the Torah. It uses the same 'by dwelling' reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is the same as חזקיה's: possessing the land happened through living on it. The difference is that this פסוק comes from the Torah itself, not from נביאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And you shall possess it and dwell there";
How did you possess it? By dwelling there.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא: וִירִשְׁתֶּם אֹתָהּ וִישַׁבְתֶּם בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel source for the same rule taught in step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 11:31 shows that land is possessed through dwelling
steps.whatToRemember: Land is acquired by חזקה, learned from פסוקים that tie 'taking' or 'possessing' land to dwelling on it.

steps.title: Where do we learn that movables are acquired only by pulling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: property that is not a guarantee (movables) is acquired only by משיכה. Then it asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And property that does not serve as a guarantee is acquired only by pulling.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's rule for movable property and asks for its source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Property without guarantee' means movables, since a creditor cannot collect from them once they are sold. The משנה says they need משיכה, pulling the item, and the גמרא wants a פסוק for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that does not serve as a guarantee, meaning movables
Pulling the item toward oneself, a way of acquiring

phrases.english: 'And property that does not serve as a guarantee'
'is acquired only by pulling.'
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת אֵין נִקְנִין אֶלָּא בִּמְשִׁיכָה. מְנָלַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from land to the משנה's rule for movables
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source showing that movables are acquired by משיכה

steps.title: 'From your neighbor's hand': acquired hand to hand
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'or buy from your neighbor's hand.' This points to something passed from hand to hand, meaning by pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And if you sell something to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor's hand.' This means an item acquired from hand to hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about selling. The words 'from your neighbor's hand' show that movables pass by a physical act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'from the hand' suggests the item moves from the seller's hand to the buyer's. That fits movables, which can be picked up and pulled, and it is the source for משיכה.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And if you sell something to your neighbor,
or buy from your neighbor's hand":
an item that is acquired from hand to hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 25:14, 'from your neighbor's hand,' shows that movables are acquired hand to hand, by משיכה

steps.title: What about רבי יוחנן, who says money acquires by Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that by Torah law, money acquires movables. So why does the משנה say movables are acquired only by pulling?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן, who says that by Torah law money acquires, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from the view of רבי יוחנן. In his view, the Torah's way to acquire movables is money, not pulling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, משיכה is only a rabbinic rule. So the משנה's word 'only by pulling' seems to leave out the Torah's own method, money. The גמרא asks how he would explain the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What can be said? (how would he explain it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. For רבי יוחנן, money is the Torah's way to acquire movables, while משיכה was set by the Rabbis.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan, who says:
by Torah law, money acquires,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה מָעוֹת קוֹנוֹת, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's rule and its source from רבי יוחנן's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that movables are acquired 'only by pulling'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If money acquires by Torah law, then משיכה is not the only way, and the משנה seems to ignore the Torah's method

steps.title: The משנה teaches the Rabbis' practical rule
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תנא of the משנה teaches the rabbinic rule, which is what people actually follow in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא teaches the rabbinic enactment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is stating the rule set by the Rabbis. That rule, משיכה, is what applies in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if money works by Torah law, the Rabbis required משיכה, so in practice money alone does not finish a purchase of movables. The משנה teaches the rule as it actually works, so it is not wrong for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Movables are acquired by משיכה. For רבי יוחנן this is a rabbinic rule, and the משנה teaches it because it is the rule in practice.

phrases.english: The tanna teaches the rabbinic enactment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains which level of law the משנה is teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must mean that by Torah law only משיכה works, which goes against רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches the rabbinic rule that is followed in practice, so it fits רבי יוחנן too

steps.title: Where do we learn that movables can be acquired along with land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה, that movables can be acquired together with land, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that property that is not a guarantee (movables) can be acquired together with land. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule in the משנה and asks where it comes from. This sets up חזקיה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה said movables need משיכה when bought alone. Now it adds a new rule: if you buy land, the movables can come along with it, using the same payment, contract, or חזקה. The גמרא wants a source for this new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that is not a guarantee, meaning movable items
Property that is a guarantee, meaning land
From where do we know these words? (asking for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted words look almost the same as the opening of step 23. But here the גמרא is pointing to the next clause of the משנה: movables can be acquired together with land.

phrases.english: Property that is not a guarantee.
phrases.notes: Only the first words are quoted. The משנה goes on: these can be acquired together with land.

phrases.english: From where do we know these words?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the משיכה discussion (steps 23-26) to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for acquiring movables together with land.

steps.title: חזקיה's source: gifts given together with fortified cities
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה brings a פסוק where a father gave his sons valuable gifts together with fortified cities, showing that movables can be passed along with land.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The פסוק says, 'And their father gave them gifts... with fortified cities in יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question with a פסוק. The gifts (movables) were given 'with' the cities (land).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'with' (עִם). The father did not hand over each gift separately. The movable gifts were transferred together with the cities, which shows that movables can be acquired along with land.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the source
And so on: the פסוק continues, but it is cut short here

steps.whatToRemember: Movables can 'ride along' with land, because the פסוק says the gifts were given 'with' the cities.

phrases.english: Hizkiyya said: Because the verse says:
"And their father gave them gifts, etc.
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב כא:ג. The skipped words list silver, gold and precious things, all movable items.

phrases.english: with fortified cities in Judah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of gifts given 'with fortified cities' shows that movables can be acquired together with land.

steps.title: Must the movables be piled on the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, for movables to be acquired along with land, they must be piled up on that land.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Do we need the movables to be piled on the land, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know movables can come along with land, the גמרא asks about a detail. Do the movables have to be sitting on the land itself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think the land acquires the movables only because they are on it, like a container. Or one could think the link is only that they are sold together, wherever the movables are. The question is which of these is true.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (an open question)

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
Do we need them piled up, or not?
phrases.notes: This means the movables piled on the land being bought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the conditions of the rule that was just given a source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether movables must be physically on the land to be acquired along with it.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins a proof from רבי עקיבא: any amount of land counts
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף starts quoting a teaching of רבי עקיבא: even the tiniest piece of land is obligated in פאה and ביכורים. The quote continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear: רבי עקיבא says, land of any size is obligated in פאה and in ביכורים...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף begins a proof to answer the question. He quotes רבי עקיבא, and the quote is not finished yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's key words are 'land of any size,' meaning even a tiny piece has the full law of land. Keep these words in mind: the rest of the quote, in the coming lines, will tie this idea to the question about piled movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is being brought)
The corner of the field left for the poor
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
Rabbi Akiva says:
Land of any amount
is obligated in pe'ah, and in first fruits,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a proof to resolve the question of step 29.
steps.raayaObject: Whether movables must be piled on the land to be acquired along with it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's teaching that land of any size is obligated in פאה and ביכורים (the quote continues).
